name: Three-touch email
when_to_use: Email is the only wired channel, or deliverability is fragile - a new sending domain, incomplete warmup, or a persona whose security tooling treats extra channels as suspicious.
rationale: Three touches maximum, each adding a new angle rather than repeating the pitch. Follow-ups are not filler: they carry 42-50% of total replies, so a single-touch campaign leaves roughly half its replies unsent. Past three the marginal reply does not justify the domain-reputation cost.

send_window.why: Materialized at send time against the contact's location. The window is a campaign rule; the timestamp is per contact.

touches.intent: Name the problem in the reader's own words and earn one reply. Nothing else.
touches.ask_note: An interest question, not a meeting. 'Is this worth exploring?' outperforms any calendar ask on touch 1.
cites: research/04 §5.3 (175-word ceiling, single CTA, no attachments on first touch)

touches.intent: Add an angle touch 1 did not use. Never restate it.
touches.ask_note: 'Mind if I send over a short summary?' - a smaller yes than a meeting, and it creates the next touch legitimately.
constraints: never reference the previous email's silence
cites: research/04 §5.2 (each follow-up adds a new angle)
research/04 §5.3 (no 'as per my last email', no guilt language)

touches.intent: Close the loop and make not-replying easy. A clean exit preserves the option to return later.

branches.why: An interested reply is not a finished deal. The meeting is not booked until it is booked.
Any reply cancels the cold sequence. A scheduled follow-up landing after a human answered is the clearest possible tell that nobody is reading.
